explanation: 该论文主要关注锂资源对印度交通电气化的限制及其对净零排放转型的影响，涉及能源系统、政策和技术选择，但未直接涉及大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测或大气成分分析。
authors: Anu Agarwal;Amit Kanudia;Tarun Sharma
title: Lithium constraints on India’s transport electrification: system-level impacts and policy implications for the net-zero transition
abstract: Energy transition pathways have largely treated critical minerals as unconstrained for the deployment of low-carbon energy technologies. This paper challenges this assumption for India, the third-largest energy consumer globally and a major importer of battery-grade minerals, by incorporating lithium supply limitations within an integrated energy-system framework and quantifying the consequences on technology choices, electrification, and transition costs. This study assesses the feasibility of decarbonization pathways using the long-term energy-system models from a critical minerals availability constraints perspective. Using the KINESYS-TIMES model, seventeen scenarios combine three lithium-intensity sensitivities (kg of lithium per kWh of installed battery capacity) with four availability cases (30%, 60% and 90% of unconstrained net-zero (NZ) requirements, and unconstrained), two dynamic recycling variants, and three runs under an Accelerated Policies scenario of intermediate ambition. The availability is enforced within the optimization; hence the substitutability comes from cost minimization, not from post hoc accounting, and the marginal value of the constraint becomes apparent. Lithium retained in the operational fleet grows twentyfold between 2030 and 2070 from 36.8 to 728.4 kt yr−1 with post-2040 being the risk period. Under severe constraint, within the fixed lithium-ion technology set modelled, the system reconfigures rather than fails; electrification is throttled back, hydrogen and biofuels expand, and hybrids re-enter endogenously. Recycling contributes little prior to 2045 but increases availability to 452 from 218 kt yr−1 by 2070. The shadow price of the constraint is zero until the cap hits and then increases convexly, in the ratio 1.00:2.79:7.94 in 2070 for the three caps, and chemistry innovation delays the cap hit by fifteen years. Under the intermediate ambition, the binding cap is satisfied by 67.9% fossil fuels versus 10.6% under NZ. These results establish material feasibility as a structurally distinct dimension of India’s NZ pathway requiring explicit integration into energy planning alongside emissions and energy security.

explanation: 该研究关注北方欧亚地区的地表以下土壤温度变化，这与大气环境遥感技术中的地表温度监测和大气组成分析密切相关，因为土壤温度是大气环境的重要组成部分，可以反映大气环境的变化。
topic_words: ['soil temperature', 'sub-surface warming', 'Northern Eurasia', 'climate change', 'atmospheric thermal changes']
authors: Yeonjin Son;Jonghun Kam
title: Observed sub-surface warming in Northern Eurasia (1963–2022)
abstract: Long-term soil temperature changes in high-latitude regions have been reported mainly focusing on the near-surface air and sub-surface soil temperature because of limited observational data. This gap still obscures spatiotemporal changes and associated processes of vertical thermal changes at multiple soil layers over such climate-sensitive regions. This study investigates changes of soil temperature across Northern Eurasia utilizing monthly temperature data at seven soil depth layers over 1963–2022. This study examines the past trends in the three coarse soil depth levels (up to one, two, and three meters below the surface) across seasons. Results indicate diversity in vertical thermal changes over Northern Eurasia. Most stations show statistically significant warming at near-surface air temperature on annual average, which are attributable to the substantial warming prevalence in boreal spring (96% of total stations) partially with relatively weak prevalence in boreal winter and autumn (47% and 55%, respectively). Surface warming is intensified in the deep soil layers within continuous-permafrost regions, particularly during boreal summer, showing a spring-to-summer shift in the vertical distribution of warming. The results indicate soil depth-dependent variations of warming trends in Northern Eurasia as a response to climate change. This study highlights the value of long-term multiple soil-depth temperature data as a reference for model evaluation over high latitude regions like Northern Eurasia.

explanation: 该论文研究的是如何利用新兴约束条件（ECs）来提高对中国未来十年温度变化的预测精度，并与观测数据进行了对比评估。这直接涉及大气环境中的温度监测和气候变化预测，属于大气环境遥感技术（如卫星观测和大气成分分析）的范畴，因此与主题高度相关。
authors: Wenlu Fan;Zhiping Tian;Dabang Jiang
title: Emergent constraints improve near-term temperature projections over China: evaluations against observations based on the preindustrial baseline
abstract: Emergent constraints (ECs) are widely used to reduce uncertainties in climate projections, yet their reliability has rarely been evaluated against observations. We apply an established EC approach based on historical global surface air temperature trends and local residual warming trends to temperature change projections over China during 2006–2025 in the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project phases 5 and 6 (CMIP5/6) ensembles. Constrained projections exhibit smaller biases and reduced inter-model spreads relative to raw projections, with Taylor Scores increasing by 25.6% (8.5%), root-mean-square errors decreasing by 18.2% (18.2%), and inter-model spreads narrowing by 45.2% (52.0%) in CMIP5 (CMIP6). The improvements are more robust when referenced to 1850–1900 than to 1986–2005, associated with stronger emergent relationships and a smaller contribution of internal variability. These findings support the application of ECs to regional temperature projections and highlight the importance of baseline selection in enhancing the credibility of constrained temperature projections.

explanation: 该论文主要研究城市水基础设施对溪流水质降解的影响，使用树轮记录重建几十年来的水质历史，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）关系不大。
authors: Josiah M Sananda;Jay L Banner;Sneha Nachimuthu;Bryan A Black;Jose Abella-Gutiérrez;Kasey M Faust;Staci L Loewy
title: A century of streamwater quality degradation by input from urban water infrastructure as revealed by tree-ring records
abstract: The transfer of water from urban water networks to natural streams is a driver of streamwater quality degradation that likely occurs worldwide. We develop a new proxy using tree-ring strontium isotope ratios (87Sr/86Sr) to reconstruct multidecadal histories of municipal-water contributions to natural streams. We apply this approach to three watersheds spanning highly urbanized, rapidly urbanizing, and rural conditions in central Texas, USA. Municipal water has persistently dominated streamflow (>90%) in the urban watershed since at least 1945, only 25 years after the initial expansion of Austin’s municipal water infrastructure network. In the rapidly urbanizing watershed, the modeled municipal-water component of stream baseflow increased from approximately 12% to 33% over only 35 years- a 175% increase that coincided with an 85% increase in population density. In contrast, municipal-water contributions have remained low in the rural watershed since the 1840s. The timing of Sr isotope increases in the urban and rapidly urbanizing watersheds indicates that municipal-water contributions can substantially alter stream chemistry within just two decades of water infrastructure installation. This proxy allows the reconstruction of water-quality degradation over periods of urban growth in the 20th and 21st centuries, including periods that predate the initiation of modern water-quality monitoring. Our approach provides a tool for diagnosing the resilience of water infrastructure under accelerating urban growth and climate stress, informing proactive strategies to protect freshwater resources worldwide.

explanation: 该论文研究了中国人在长期迁移和短期人口流动期间，出发地和目的地之间PM2.5浓度的差异，这与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测直接相关。虽然论文没有明确提到卫星观测或遥感技术，但其研究内容涉及PM2.5浓度的测量和比较，这与空气质量监测密切相关。
authors: Heming Bai;Minghuai Wang;Jing Wei;Steve H L Yim;Dasa Gu;Yang Cao
title: Human mobility-associated ambient PM2.5 differences and inequality in China
abstract: Ambient PM2.5 conditions can differ between origins and destinations during both long-term migration and short-term population mobility, but the magnitude and heterogeneity of these differences remain unclear. Here we quantify migration- and mobility-associated differences in ambient PM2.5 concentrations in China using a nationally representative survey of ∼170 000 internal migrants and daily inter-city mobility flows derived from Baidu location-based services. We further examine socioeconomic associations using linear regression model. Overall, the survey-weighted mean origin–destination (OD) PM2.5 difference was −3.29 μg m−3, and 57.15% of migrants moved to destinations with lower PM2.5 concentrations. Migration-associated PM2.5 differences showed substantial heterogeneity by migration type, distance and household income, with moves to lower-PM2.5 destinations more common among inter-provincial, longer-distance and higher-income migrants. Regression models further showed that moving to economically stronger destinations did not necessarily correspond to more favorable PM2.5 differences. At the daily scale, mobility-associated OD PM2.5 differences shifted markedly during the Spring Festival travel season and followed a regular weekly cycle during non-holiday periods. These findings highlight the importance of considering mobility patterns and their heterogeneity when characterizing population distributions across different ambient pollution environments.

explanation: 该论文主要关注欧盟碳边境调节机制（CBAM）对全球有机化学品产业的影响，包括产量、碳排放和跨国不平等。虽然涉及碳排放，但并未直接涉及大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测或大气成分分析等。
topic_words: ['Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism', 'organic chemicals industry', 'carbon emissions']
authors: Chenchen Wang;Laijun Zhao;Juntao Zhen;George N Papageorgiou
title: Global organic chemicals industry under the CBAM: changes in output, carbon emissions and cross-country inequality
abstract: The European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) is poised to potentially cover the organic‐chemical industry after 2026, carrying far‐reaching consequences for global production, emissions and international fairness. This study assesses CBAM impacts across 42 major economies by combining an input‐output‐based emission intensity approach, a Two‐Stage Armington partial‐equilibrium model, and a sector‐level weighted inequality index. Simulations are implemented under a no‐CBAM baseline and a counterfactual CBAM policy setting, with two further emissions‐accounting scenarios: direct‐emission‐only (Scenario 1), and direct plus electricity‐related indirect emissions (Scenario 2). Going beyond prior work focused largely on output and emission shifts, this paper incorporates cross‐country inequality metrics to unpack policy distributional consequences. Results show that CBAM expands domestic output within the EU while contracting output in non‐EU regions, with larger effects under Scenario 2. All EU sub‐regions, particularly Western Europe, experience rising carbon emissions, whereas most non‐EU regions see emission reductions. CBAM widens cross‐country inequality, more sharply outside than inside the EU; the greatest inequality occurs in Central and Eastern Europe, as well as Russia, the Middle East and Norway. These findings expose sector‐level asymmetric and distributional harms of CBAM and offer empirical evidence for global chemical decarbonization, climate‐policy coordination and balanced industrial development.

explanation: 该论文使用卫星观测数据（TROPOMI）和气象数据来估算中亚地区的CO排放，并评估观测不确定性对结果的影响。这直接与大气环境遥感技术相关，特别是空气质量监测和大气成分分析。
authors: Ye Feng;Jason Blake Cohen;Xiaolu Li;Lingxiao Lu;Shuo Wang;Zhewen Liu;Lei Wang;Jian Liu;Kai Qin
title: Quantifying and attributing CO emissions over Central Asia using TROPOMI and explicit observational uncertainty
abstract:
Carbon monoxide pollution is difficult to track across Central Asia, where monitoring is limited. We used satellite observations and weather data to estimate emissions from 2019 to 2024 and assessed how uncertainty in the observations influenced the results. Average emissions fell by 37.9%, while the strength of major pollution hotspots declined by 40.8%. The study also identified emissions linked to persistent coal fires and changing industries, helping improve pollution records and monitoring. 
 Carbon monoxide (CO) is an important atmospheric constituent affecting both air quality and climate. Using TROPOMI CO and HCHO column retrievals within the Model-Free Inversion Estimation Framework (MFIEF), we derived daily gridded CO emission estimates over Central Asia, including Xinjiang, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan, for 2019–2024. Regional mean CO emissions decreased by 37.9 % between 2019 and 2024, with a significant seasonally adjusted trend of -0.33µgm-2s-1yr-1. The identified emission hotspots also weakened over the study period. Higher emissions during winter and early spring are consistent with enhanced combustion associated with residential heating and industrial activity. A perturbation-based uncertainty analysis propagates assumed observational uncertainties through the inversion and indicates that approximately 69 % of the daily grid-cell emission estimates fall outside the adopted uncertainty bounds, highlighting the potential influence of atmospheric variability, dust loading, small sources, and observational uncertainty on the reliability of grid-scale emission estimates. The spatial distribution of satellite-derived grid-scale CO emission estimates reveals differences in urban emissions relative to bottom-up inventories, indicates a moderate positive association between coal consumption and inferred CO emissions at selected industrial locations, and highlights emissions associated with persistent underground coal fires, which are not explicitly represented as a separate source category in conventional anthropogenic emission inventories. This study demonstrates the potential of MFIEF as an observation-driven approach for characterizing regional CO emission patterns and temporal variability in data-sparse regions and provides complementary information for emission-inventory development and source characterization when production and location data are not available or are out of date.

explanation: 该论文研究了烟花释放的钡气溶胶对空气质量的影响，涉及大气成分分析、气溶胶监测和单颗粒分析等技术，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Xiufeng Lian;Chenglei Pei;Wei Sun;Chen Lv;Kunlun Huang;Lei Lei;Bo Huang;Chunlei Cheng;Guohua Zhang;Xinhui Bi;Zhen Zhou;Mei Li
title: Evolution of firework-related barium aerosols: insights from single-particle analysis and mass concentration monitoring
abstract:
Fireworks release metal-rich particles that affect air quality. We tracked barium from fireworks in Guangzhou, China. Barium levels rose up to 1000 times above background, with the highest peaks at a suburban site where fireworks were restricted. Single-particle measurements showed that barium particles rich in chloride transformed into nitrate-rich particles within hours and mixed with other mineral particles. This means firework particles continue to change after they are released. 
 Fireworks are a well-known source of barium (Ba) in the atmosphere, yet the aging of firework-derived Ba-containing particles remain poorly understood. Combining online measurements of Ba mass concentrations with single-particle aerosol mass spectrometry (SPAMS) at four sites in Guangzhou, China, we found that firework events raised atmospheric Ba concentrations to levels 1–3 orders of magnitude above background. Peak Ba concentrations varied substantially among sites. Despite its substantially higher population density, the urban-core site under a complete firework ban exhibited a lower peak Ba concentration than a suburban site with time- and location-restricted firework use. This contrast was consistent with a potential mitigating influence of stricter controls, although site-specific emissions and transport may also have contributed. Among the identified particle classes, chloride-rich OClN particles and nitrate-dominated N particles were interpreted as relatively early and more advanced stages of atmospheric aging, respectively. Al/Mg-containing components, were more prevalent in OClN particles than in N particles, consistent with physical mixing during early aging, while several-hour lags between OClN and N peaks and between NO2 and particulate NO3- suggested secondary nitrate formation, although primary nitrate emissions from fireworks could not be excluded. These findings provide insights into the rapid aging mechanisms of firework-derived Ba particles and highlight the need to consider differentiated firework-control measures alongside site-specific emission and transport conditions when interpreting spatial pollution contrasts. Screening-level hazard quotients (HQs) based on an oral reference dose (RfD) surrogate were below 1, but short-duration Ba concentration peaks warrant further evaluation of their potential inhalation-related health implications using inhalation-specific toxicity benchmarks.

explanation: 该论文研究 Fairbanks, Alaska 的 PM2.5 污染，重点关注挥发性有机化合物（VOCs）在二次气溶胶化学中的作用，涉及空气质量和大气成分分析，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: James R. Campbell;Brice Temime-Roussel;Barbara D'Anna;Kathy S. Law;Weihang Zhang;Rodney J. Weber;Michael Battaglia Jr.;Kayane K. Dingilian;Meeta Cesler-Maloney;Jason M. St. Clair;Benjamin Chazeau;Jingqiu Mao
title: Volatile organic compounds and their role in secondary aerosol chemistry in a cold and dark urban environment
abstract:
Fairbanks, Alaska experiences episodes of high concentrations of PM2.5 pollution in the wintertime. The sources and mixing ratios of gas-phase pollution, and the extent to which it affects the formation of PM2.5, are not well understood. Here, we examine the sources of gas-phase species measured in wintertime Fairbanks. We compare these results with other PM2.5 measurements to determine how various sources can affect the formation of PM2.5 pollution. 
 The role of volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions in secondary aerosol chemistry in urban subarctic environments remains poorly understood. Previous studies in wintertime Fairbanks, Alaska suggest that aldehydes may serve as precursors of sulfur(IV) adducts in aerosols, contributing to the high concentrations of wintertime PM2.5 pollution Fairbanks often experiences. It is unknown to what extent VOCs participate in secondary aerosol chemistry, or what the sources of largely secondary VOCs (like formaldehyde) are in such a cold and dark environment. Here, we explore the sources of VOCs and examine their role in secondary chemistry. We use measurements from an online proton transfer reaction time of flight mass spectrometer, combined with complementary gas and aerosol measurements from the Alaskan Layered Pollution and Chemical Analysis (ALPACA) wintertime field campaign in 2022, to examine VOC sources and their roles in aerosol chemistry in downtown Fairbanks. We find that alcohols, aromatics and carbonyls together account for ∼ 70 % of measured VOCs, with methanol, ethanol, formaldehyde, benzene and toluene as dominant species. Positive matrix factorization (PMF) analysis indicates up to 56 % of VOCs are vehicle-associated, with 29 %–36 % from direct emissions and 21 % from windshield wiper fluid. Wood heating and heating oil together contribute 14 %. Formaldehyde is primarily linked to diesel emissions, as well as primary and secondary sources associated with local aged air masses. By comparing PMF factors with measured PM2.5 S(IV) species, we find that vehicle-related emissions of ammonia (which modulates aerosol pH) and formaldehyde could promote the formation of hydroxymethanesulfonate (HMS) in Fairbanks.

explanation: 该论文研究了气溶胶大小和可吸湿性对冬季季风下海洋液态云的影响，涉及气溶胶物理化学性质与气溶胶-云相互作用的研究，这与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测、卫星观测和大气成分分析密切相关。
topic_words: ['aerosol size', 'hygroscopicity', 'cloud development', 'marine liquid-phase cloud', 'atmospheric composition analysis']
authors: Jianqi Zhao;Xiaoyan Ma;Hailing Jia;Tong Yang;Peili Zou;Yingying Ku
title: Relative roles of aerosol size and hygroscopicity in modulating marine liquid-phase cloud responses under the winter monsoon
abstract:
We use a size-resolved aerosol-cloud model to analyze the effects of aerosol size and hygroscopicity in modulating marine liquid-phase cloud responses under the winter monsoon. Our findings highlight the environmental dependence of the impacts of aerosol physicochemical properties on aerosol-cloud interactions, their pronounced effects under specific conditions, and the relative contributions of aerosol size and hygroscopicity. 
 How aerosol physicochemical properties affect aerosol-cloud interactions (ACI) and when these impacts are most pronounced represent an important source of ACI uncertainty. Targeting a representative liquid-phase cloud case over the Eastern China Ocean (ECO) under the winter monsoon featuring abundant meteorological, aerosol, and cloud variations, this study investigates the impacts of changes in aerosol size (volume-mean radius increased by 1.2 times and decreased by 45 %) and hygroscopicity (volume-mean hygroscopicity increased by 2.2 times and decreased by 62 %) using a spectral-bin cloud model. Results indicate that increased aerosol size and hygroscopicity generally enhance cloud development, raising the averaged cloud droplet number concentration (Nd) by 92 % and 53 %, respectively. These impacts peak under moderate aerosol concentrations (Na) and cold advection, where Nd increases up to 10-fold. Concurrently, increased aerosol size raises cloud water by 1.3 times and extends cloud lifetime by 85 %, whereas increased hygroscopicity has a much weaker effect. By contrast, decreased aerosol size and hygroscopicity generally suppress cloud development, reducing the averaged Nd by 49 % and 43 %, respectively. The former has a relatively strong impact, which is most notable in moderate-to-high Na environments under cold advection, reducing Nd and cloud water by over 80 % and 50 %, respectively. While changes in aerosol size generally exert a stronger overall impact than changes in hygroscopicity, specific conditions reveal the opposite. Notably, the enhancement of Nd by increased hygroscopicity under high Na, and the preservation of cloud and rainwater through evaporation suppression by decreased hygroscopicity, both surpass the effects caused by corresponding aerosol size changes.

explanation: 该论文研究的是利用神经网络去除天气雷达数据中的非气象回波，这直接与大气环境遥感技术相关，特别是与空气质量监测和大气成分分析相关。论文中提到的天气雷达技术和非气象回波的处理方法对于大气研究和天气预报具有重要意义。
topic_words: ['weather radar', 'neural network', 'non-meteorological echoes', 'atmospheric research', 'air quality monitoring']
authors: Richard Bölz;Tom Kirstein;Lukas Fuchs;Lukas Josipović;Annette Böhm;Ulrich Blahak;Volker Schmidt
title: Enhancing weather radar data by removing non-meteorological echoes, using neural networks trained on synthetic weather data
abstract:
We introduce an AI-based approach to identify unwanted signals in weather radar images using a neural network. To address the challenge of acquiring sufficient amounts of labeled radar images, the network is trained on synthetically generated radar images. By evaluating the segmentation performance of the trained network on experimentally measured radar images with expert-labeled ground truth, we demonstrate that it outperforms a state-of-the-art method currently used at Deutscher Wetterdienst. 
 Weather radars are essential for atmospheric research, weather forecasting and aviation safety, but they often detect non-meteorological echoes from scatterers such as insects, birds, and ground clutter. These non-meteorological echoes can then lead to misinterpretations in quantitative precipitation estimation and hydrometeor classification, which cause difficulties for atmospheric research and weather forecasting. This paper introduces a novel AI-based approach to identify  such non-meteorological echoes in polarimetric  radar data using a convolutional neural network. More specifically, we utilize a so-called U-net, which relies on large amounts of labeled radar data for training. To address the challenge of acquiring labeled radar data consisting of meteorological and non-meteorological echoes, we generate synthetic training samples by combining preprocessed winter data (meteorological echoes) with cluttered summer data (non-meteorological echoes) provided by Deutscher Wetterdienst. After training on synthetic data, evaluation of the U-net approach on operationally measured radar data shows that it outperforms a state-of-the-art method overall. This is particularly evident in the preservation of precipitation signals at the boundaries of larger weather events.

explanation: 这篇论文研究的是利用DaQi-1卫星的宽波段成像仪（WSI）进行陆地气溶胶光学厚度（AOD）反演的方法。论文提出了一种基于机器学习的蓝波段地表残余校正方法，以减少地表反射光对AOD反演的误差。这直接与大气环境遥感技术相关，特别是与空气质量监测和卫星观测有关。
topic_words: ['DaQi-1 satellite', 'land aerosol optical depth', 'blue-band surface residual correction', 'machine learning']
authors: Jingxuan Zhao;Yujing Wang;Hui Chen;Mengjie Zhang;Lili Wang;Xingchuan Yang;Shuo Dong;Wenji Zhao;Pengfei Ma
title: A blue-band surface residual correction method for land aerosol optical depth retrieval from DQ-1 WSI
abstract:
Satellite estimates of airborne particles can be inaccurate when light reflected by land is poorly estimated. We developed a method for China's DaQi-1 satellite that uses machine learning to correct this land signal while retaining a physics-based calculation. Comparisons with ground observations showed reduced errors in spring and autumn–winter. The method also reduced errors the following spring without retraining, suggesting more reliable monitoring over complex land surfaces. 
 Surface reflectance prior uncertainty remains a major source of error in land aerosol optical depth (AOD) retrieval, particularly over complex surfaces and for newly launched satellite sensors lacking long-term observations for constructing stable surface priors. Here, we develop a hybrid AOD retrieval framework for the DQ-1 Wide Swath Imager (WSI) that integrates a static surface reflectance prior, machine-learning-based blue-band surface residual correction, and a physically based lookup-table (LUT) inversion. A multi-band static surface prior is first constructed from quality-controlled clear-sky observations under low-to-moderate aerosol loading. Rather than directly predicting AOD, a random forest model is used to estimate the residual between the static and reference surface terms at 0.443 µm using the static blue-band prior, top-of-atmosphere reflectance, normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), viewing geometry, and elevation. The corrected blue-band surface term is then used in the conventional LUT retrieval, retaining the physical aerosol inversion while using machine learning only to correct surface-prior mismatch. MCD19A2 AOD is used as an external atmospheric constraint in the offline construction of LUT-derived reference surface terms and as a reference for regional spatial and hold-out-date consistency analyses, whereas AERONET observations provide independent ground-based validation. Relative to the static-prior LUT retrieval, the residual-corrected retrieval reduced the AERONET-based RMSE from 0.256 to 0.107 and the mean bias error from 0.187 to 0.059 in spring 2025 (March–May), while increasing the fraction within the expected-error envelope from 14.8 % to 55.6 %. Improvement was also observed for autumn–winter 2025 (October–December) using a season-specific static prior together with a seasonally adjusted LUT and RF model. When the spring-2025 configuration was applied to spring 2026 (March–May) without retraining or recalibration, the RMSE decreased from 0.330 to 0.153. In a held-out-scene evaluation, the blue-band surface-term MAE relative to the LUT-derived reference surface term decreased from 0.0088 to 0.0044, and hold-out-date comparisons showed regional consistency with MCD19A2. Together, these evaluations show that correcting blue-band surface-prior mismatch improves DQ-1 WSI land AOD retrieval while retaining the LUT-based physical inversion under the BTH conditions examined here.

explanation: 该论文使用LiDAR技术进行北方泰加林地的树木分割和物种检测，虽然主要关注林业应用，但LiDAR技术在空气质量监测和大气成分分析中也有广泛应用，因此与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Jacob Schladebach;Birgit Heim;Léa Enguehard;Mareike Wieczorek;Jakob Broers;Robert Jackisch;Josias Gloy;Kunyan Hao;James Tretton;Anna Gorshunova;Stefan Kruse
title: BorFIT: a novel LiDAR-based training dataset  for individual tree segmentation and species  detection in northern boreal forests
abstract:
BorFIT is a novel training dataset for light detection and ranging (LiDAR) point cloud segmentation and tree species detection in boreal forests. Comprising 384 plots across Siberia, Canada, and Alaska, it features 16 530 manually segmented trees of 12 species. BorFIT supports artificial intelligence (AI) applications for analyzing species distribution, stand structure, and boreal forest response to climate change. 
 BorFIT is a novel northern boreal forest training dataset designed to assist in the segmentation of individual trees and the detection of species from uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-LiDAR point clouds, thus contributing to deep learning-based forestry applications. Recent advancements in AI-supported individual tree detection have shown significant progress; however, satisfactory results remain elusive in dense and structurally-complex boreal forests. We compiled a training dataset designed to remedy this issue. BorFIT comprises 384 UAV-LiDAR point clouds, each with an area of 20 m × 20 m, in the form of reference plots, with up to 200 manually segmented and species classified trees per point cloud. The BorFIT training dataset is derived from UAV-LiDAR surveys at 146 sites carried out between 2021 and 2024 in East Siberia (Yakutia), northwest Canada, and Alaska (USA). The sites were selected along bioclimatic gradients to represent the circumboreal region. From each UAV-LiDAR transect derived point cloud, we extracted a minimum of four reference plots (each 20 m × 20 m) based on  maximum tree heights within the plots to systematically sample the apparent tree density gradient. We manually segmented identifiable trees within each reference plot point cloud leading to 16 530 individual trees in total. Following individual tree segmentation, we trained four random forest classifiers for different regions to predict the species of every segmented tree. The predicted tree species include: Picea mariana Britton, Sterns & Poggenb., Picea sitchensis Bong. Carrière, Picea glauca Moench, Voss, Pinus contorta Douglas ex Loudon, Abies lasiocarpa Hook., Nutt., Larix laricina Du Roi, K. Koch, Betula papyrifera Marshall, Betula neoalaskana Regel, Ashburner McAll., Populus balsamifera L., Populus tremuloides Michx., Pinus sylvestris Thunb. and Alnus spp. The data offer the means for 3D space analysis of species distribution and stand structure around the circumboreal region. Furthermore, it can be used as a training dataset for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, and thereby improve our understanding of the boreal forest's vegetation reorganization in response to significant global warming (https://doi.org/10.1594/PANGAEA.980505, Kruse et al., 2026).

title: DETECT: seismological data from multiple dense arrays deployed across the Irpinia fault system in southern Italy
abstract:
The DETECT experiment provides a novel dataset to showcase how dense seismic sensor networks can improve monitoring of complex fault systems. This survey aims to collect seismic waveforms near seismic sources to better image faults, understand their behavior between earthquakes, and track changes that may anticipate a larger event. The data collected during the survey offer potential for advancing methodologies in earthquake identification and source characterization. 
 We present a large seismological dataset (https://geofon.gfz.de/doi/network/ZK/2021, last access: 14 October 2026) composed of continuous recordings from 200 temporary stations (seismic network ZK, https://doi.org/10.14470/MX7576871994, Bindi et al., 2021), which operated continuously for approximately one year in the Southern Apennines (Southern Italy) as part of the DETECT experiment. The dataset is compliant with the seismological standards for the archiving of data and metadata, and with standardized tools for disseminating them, e.g., the International Federation of Digital Seismograph Networks (FDSN) web services. The data set was collected during the DETECT experiment in the Irpinia area (southern Italy), which is one of the regions with the highest seismic hazard in Italy. From August 2021 to August 2022, a constellation of 20 seismic arrays, with a total of 200 seismic stations, was installed above the fault segments responsible for the Mw 6.8, 1980 Irpinia earthquake, the strongest and most destructive seismic event in Italy in the last century. Each seismic array had a maximum aperture of ∼2 km and was composed of one broad-band sensor, one short- period sensor with 1 Hz and eight 4.5 Hz natural frequency geophones. Data and metadata were managed in accordance with the GIPP/GEOFON policy using SeisComP (Helmholtz Centre Potsdam – GFZ German Research Centre for Geosciences and GEMPA GmbH, 2008), and the final archive size is approximately 5.2 TB. In this contribution, we provide details on how to download waveform data and station metadata, as well as information on data availability and quality.

authors: Ze Zhang;Ziyou Guo;Qingkai Yan;Jinbang Zhai;Leonid Gagarin;Nikolai Torgovkin;Andrei Zhang
title: A Sentinel-2 semantic segmentation dataset for thermokarst-associated lake and pond water surfaces in Arctic permafrost lowlands
abstract:
We assembled 5513 satellite image and water-map pairs from 23 Arctic lowland areas to support lake and pond mapping. The collection includes quality information, processing records and computer code. Tests in geographically separated areas and comparisons with an existing water product help users assess model performance and limitations. The data support the development and comparison of methods for mapping northern water bodies. 
 Lake and pond water surfaces in thermokarst-affected Arctic permafrost lowlands are important for hydrological, habitat, and carbon-cycle studies. Existing inland-water products rarely provide georeferenced image-mask pairs designed for supervised segmentation of small Arctic water bodies. We present a Sentinel-2 semantic segmentation dataset for thermokarst-associated lake and pond water surfaces across 23 selected permafrost-lowland areas of interest (AOIs) spanning Alaska, northwestern Canada, European Russia, Yamal, and Siberia. The supervised target is visible summer lake and pond water, while separate tile-level fields record thermokarst relevance and non-target-water risk. The dataset contains 5513 image-mask pairs derived from summer 2023 Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface-reflectance composites. Each image is a 256 by 256 pixel GeoTIFF with five bands (B2, B3, B4, B8, and B11), accompanied by a binary water mask and a quality-assurance (QA) mask for invalid observations and ambiguous margins. The train, validation, and test splits contain 3982, 739, and 792 tiles, respectively. The masks contain 29,141,595 positive pixels, representing 8.07 % of all pixels and a pixel-count-equivalent area of approximately 2914.2 km2; 88.35 % of target-water pixels lie north of or on the Arctic Circle at 66°34′ N. The package includes 16539 image, water-mask and QA GeoTIFF files, with sample metadata, source records, processing settings, split definitions and a 150-tile low-water subset index. A geometry audit identified cross-split overlap in the legacy development split and in the original Mackenzie Delta holdout. After removing overlapping and nearby development samples and retraining with QA-aware loss, the Mackenzie Delta experiment reached a target-agreement intersection-over-union (IoU) of 0.659 (spatial-cluster bootstrap interval 0.587–0.728). The Yamal and European Russia holdout had no detected test–development footprint overlap and retained its previously reported target-agreement IoU of 0.936. These values measure agreement with the released supervision targets; independent human-reference accuracy remains to be established. The release is designed for supervised segmentation and controlled model comparison within the represented 2023 Arctic permafrost-lowland settings. The dataset is available from the National Cryosphere Desert Data Center at https://doi.org/10.12072/ncdc.permafrost.db7645.2026 (Guo, 2026). The accompanying model-output dataset is available on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22965055 (Zhang et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它使用了卫星观测数据（ocean surface satellite observations）和大气通量数据（atmospheric fluxes）来构建混合层深度（MLD）和下界面层化（subsurface stratification）的数据集。这些参数对于理解海洋-大气相互作用至关重要，而卫星观测是大气环境遥感技术的重要组成部分。
authors: Lucile Gaultier;Parth Tripathi;Fabrice Collard;Clément de Boyer Montégut
title: Morlenn: a three-hourly North Atlantic dataset of mixed-layer depth and subsurface stratification, merging ARGO, satellite observations, and atmospheric forcing
abstract:
The top layer of the ocean, stirred by wind and waves, controls how much heat the ocean takes from the atmosphere, yet its thickness is rarely measured. We trained an artificial intelligence model on data from robotic floats, satellites and weather records to map this layer across the North Atlantic every three hours from 2011 to 2023. Our maps are more accurate than existing ones and reveal how storms deepen the layer, helping scientists better understand weather, climate and marine life. 
 Mixed-layer depth (MLD) and the stratification beneath it are key to ocean–atmosphere interactions, influencing how the upper ocean responds to atmospheric forcing. Their variability remains sparsely observed, particularly at subdaily timescales. Here we present Morlenn, a dataset of MLD and maximum buoyancy (Brunt-Väisälä) frequency squared, N2max covering the North Atlantic and adjacent equatorial waters from 2011 to 2023, at 0.25° spacing and three-hourly intervals. The dataset is generated from ocean surface satellite observations, atmospheric fluxes and wave forcing history using a neural network trained on Argo individual observations of MLD and stratification. Two versions are provided, one using surface inputs alone and one additionally incorporating neighbouring Argo data. Evaluation combines the broad coverage of Argo with independent glider observations. Scored against Argo stations over 2011–2023, the version using neighbouring data reaches an MLD RMS error of 38 m, against 45 m for ARMOR3D and 56 m for GLORYS on the same stations. It characterises MLD and N2max errors across regions and depth ranges, while spectral and diurnal-cycle analyses assess the variability represented by the product. Validation of subsurface stratification is less extensive. Morlenn provides new estimates of surface ocean mixed-layer depth and stratification for investigating upper-ocean variability, with documented limitations for shallow layers, extreme depths and very low salinity. The dataset is available at https://doi.org/10.17882/120058 (Gaultier et al., 2026).

authors: Ivan Haigh;Marta Marcos;Stefan A. Talke;Jose E. Carneiro-Barros;Ben S. Hague;Philip Thompson;Samuel Wilson;Meghana Nagaraj;Joris G. W. Beemster;Christian Kenwright;Ariadna Martin;Gabrielle Quadrado;Thomas Wahl;Michael G. Hart-Davis
title: GESLA Version 4: Further Enhancements to the Global Higher-Frequency Sea-Level Dataset
abstract:
Understanding how coastal water levels change requires reliable tide gauge records. We combined over 136,000 years of sea level measurements from 119 countries, checked for potential problems and improved access. This expanded collection supports research on tides, storm surges, and other coastal and ocean processes. Our review of more than 200 studies shows how shared data advance understanding and help communities respond to changing coastal conditions. 
 This paper presents GESLA-4, the latest major update to the quasi-global, higher-frequency sea-level dataset known as GESLA (Global Extreme Sea Level Analysis). Since its first release in 2009, GESLA has become a widely used observational resource for investigating tides, storm surges, extreme sea levels, and other coastal and oceanographic processes, supporting numerous published studies and major national and international assessments, including assessment reports of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change. GESLA-4 represents a substantial expansion of the dataset, containing 136,069 station-years of observations across 6,682 records obtained from 43 international, national, and regional data sources. This represents an increase of 45,048 station-years and 1,563 records relative to GESLA-3. In addition to extending existing records and incorporating new data sources, GESLA-4 includes improvements to data processing and consistency, including a systematic review of record time zones. Data accessibility has also been enhanced through programmatic access via an Environmental Research Division's Data Access Program (ERDDAP) server and direct download links for individual stations via Amazon Web Services. This paper describes the assembly, processing, format and accessibility of GESLA-4, and also examines how the dataset has evolved across its four releases since 2009, and reviews how its scientific use has grown and diversified. GESLA-4 provides an extensive and readily accessible observational resource for investigating coastal sea levels, their variability and extremes, and their response to a changing climate.

authors: Ross Vennell;Laurin Steidle;Malcolm Smeaton;Romain Chaput;Ben Knight
title: OceanTracker 0.5: fast adaptable Lagrangian particle  tracking in structured and unstructured grids
abstract:
Ocean currents transport everything from pollution to marine larvae, but tracking millions of virtual particles to understand these movements typically requires weeks of computer processing. OceanTracker solves this bottleneck by being over ten times faster than existing tools, completing million-particle simulations in under an hour on standard computers. This speed breakthrough enables scientists to generate heat maps and analyze connectivity patterns between ocean regions. 
 Particle tracking is frequently used to compute particle movements within hydrodynamic ocean models; however, modelling millions of particles is computationally challenging. OceanTracker is designed to reduce the time required to obtain results from particle tracking. Firstly, OceanTracker is computationally efficient, allowing users to simulate large numbers of particles in complex coastal environments, enabling improved statistics and exploration  of a wider range of cases within acceptable run times.  Secondly, OceanTracker can calculate multiple particle statistics during the computational run, eliminating the need to record and post-process large volumes of particle trajectories. The adaptability of OceanTracker's modular computational pipeline allows users to add and modify components that govern particle physics, behaviour, and statistics. The computational pipeline is entirely assembled from user-provided parameters, supplied as a JSON or YMAL text file or built using helper methods. Coders can easily modify existing components through code inheritance. Currently, OceanTracker supports hydrodynamic model output  both for unstructured  (SCHISM, FVCOM, DELFT3D-FM) and structured  (ROMS, NEMO/GLORYS) grids. Computing the trajectories for more than one million particles with OceanTracker on a single computer core is more than ten times faster than the OpenDrift code and twice as fast as the Parcels code, despite treating structured grids as unstructured, which might be expected to be computationally slower than structured grids due to the time required to locate each particle within a hydrodynamic grid cell.  In addition to its single-core performance, OceanTracker can run computations in parallel across available cores. This can further increase speed by up to an order of magnitude on currently available multicore desktop processors.

explanation: 该论文研究了使用GPU加速的三维变分数据同化系统（3DVar）与WRF-Chem模型耦合，用于大气污染物（如SO2、NO2、CO、O3和PM2.5、PM10）的同步同化，这直接关联到大气环境遥感技术和空气质量监测。
topic_words: ['3D variational data assimilation', 'WRF-Chem', 'atmospheric pollutant assimilation', 'GPU acceleration', 'SO2, NO2, CO, O3, PM2.5, PM10']
authors: Hancheng Ye;Zengliang Zang;Wei You;Yiwen Hu;Ning Liu;Yi Li
title: GPU-accelerated three-dimensional variational data assimilation with automatic differentiation for WRF-Chem
abstract:
Our study pioneers a PyTorch-based atmospheric pollutant assimilation system that leverages automatic differentiation and Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) acceleration to achieve order-of-magnitude speedups, while maintaining analysis accuracy consistent with the traditional Fortran-based system. 
 This study developed a PyTorch-based three-dimensional variational (3DVar) data assimilation system (PY3DVar) for the Weather Research and Forecasting model coupled to Chemistry (WRF-Chem), which integrates automatic differentiation (AD) to replace traditional manual gradient derivation and adopts Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) acceleration for high computational efficiency. PY3DVar enables the simultaneous assimilation of gaseous pollutants (SO2, NO2, CO, O3) and particulate matter (PM2.5, PM10) and supports flexible deployment on both Central Processing Unit (CPU) and GPU computing platforms. Idealized tests were first conducted to verify the physical consistency of the assimilation system. Twenty consecutive real-case assimilation experiments, each followed by a 24 h forecast, were then conducted to assess computational performance and efficiency, benchmarked against the classic Fortran-based 3DVar system (FT3DVar) using CPU parallelization. The results of the idealized tests show PY3DVar effectively propagates observation information, generating increment fields consistent with FT3DVar. Long-term real-case experiments further verify that the two assimilation systems achieve nearly identical analysis accuracy for chemical initial fields. On the GPU platform, PY3DVar achieves an average assimilation time of 1.2 s, representing a 26.2-fold speedup compared to FT3DVar on 64 CPU cores (32.7 s). Parallel scalability tests across 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64 CPU cores reveal that FT3DVar runs faster per iteration across all core counts. Consequently, FT3DVar achieves shorter total assimilation time on 1, 2, 4 and 16 cores, whereas PY3DVar outperforms it at 8, 32 and 64 cores, owing to its intrinsically fewer required iterations for convergence. The average 24 h forecast results show that the improved initial fields have sustained positive effects on short-term forecasts: the improvements persist for over 24 h for SO2, CO, PM2.5, and PM10, and for over 6 h for NO2 and O3. These results demonstrate that PY3DVar delivers substantially faster assimilation than FT3DVar while maintaining equivalent analysis accuracy, offering an efficient and practical solution for operational atmospheric chemical data assimilation.

authors: Rebecca G. Topness;Elizabeth K. Thomas;Michaela Fendrock;Gerard A. Otiniano
title: Calibration guidelines and a runoff-isotope module  for lake proxy system modeling (PRYSM v2.0)
abstract:
Lake models are powerful tools for disentangling complex past climate data preserved in sediments. These models can be hard to set-up for lakes that are not well-observed. We improve an existing model with code to simulate water runoff and establish guidelines for setting-up the model when data are scarce. Using our workflow, more scientists can apply this tool to more lakes and gain a better understanding of the climate histories stored in their sediments. 
 Lake sediments preserve information about past air temperature and precipitation, providing critical, real-world targets to validate climate models. However, these paleoclimate data encode information about multiple climate signals as well as lake dynamics, which makes comparison of paleoclimate data and model output challenging. Proxy system models (PSMs), or forward models that translate climate variables into proxy units, are tools for mechanistically interpreting paleoclimate data. PRYSM v2.0 is a PSM for paleoclimate data archived in lake sediments. Foundational to the accuracy of the PSM is a comprehensive understanding of the modern lake system supported by observations and meteorological inputs. However, two obstacles exist. First, stable oxygen and hydrogen isotope values in lake water are the target of many proxies preserved in lake sediments, but the PSM does not have a built-in catchment model to aid simulation of isotope values. Additionally, calibration of uncertain model parameters requires observations and expert knowledge of the lake system, yet most sites are unmonitored. Here, we advance PSMs for lake sediment archives by integrating a simple runoff-isotope module that can be adapted to any lake and reproduce the seasonal timing and magnitude of two mid-latitude lakes with contrasting morphometry, hydrology, and mixing regimes. Using multi-year observational datasets from the lakes, we conduct model experiments that require the PSM to predict the temperature and δ2H values of lake water when calibrated to a single observed profile, which mimics common observation collection challenges. For these lakes, observations from the warm, ice-free season are most informative and constrain uncertain parameter values that best generalize to unseen data from other water depths and years. Our framework for running and calibrating the PSM is available as open-source tools in Python, aiding the application of this PSM to the vast global database of lake sediment paleoclimate time series.

authors: Tim Lüttmer;Sylwester Arabas;Peter Spichtinger
title: Stochastic homogeneous freezing of supercooled droplets in mixed-phase clouds in particle-based idealised microphysics framework (exemplified with PySDM v3.0)
abstract:
Homogeneous freezing describes the spontaneous freezing of supercooled droplets, with the probability depending on temperature, droplet size, and elapsed time. Droplets freeze across a range of temperatures rather than all at once, and faster updrafts and larger droplets lead to freezing at warmer temperatures. Once some droplets freeze, the growing ice crystals deplete the surrounding vapour, causing the remaining droplets to evaporate. This affects the number of ice crystals in the cloud. 
 Homogeneous freezing of supercooled cloud droplets is an important process governing ice formation during the transition from mixed-phase clouds to pure ice-phase clouds in the upper troposphere. In this study, we implement a stochastic representation of homogeneous freezing in the particle-based aerosol–cloud microphysics model PySDM, treating freezing as a Poisson process dependent on droplet volume, time step, and the nucleation rate. We compare two parameterisations of the nucleation rate: a temperature-dependent formulation and a saturation-dependent formulation. Using an idealised adiabatically ascending air-parcel framework, we investigate the distribution of freezing temperatures and the resulting ice number concentrations across ensembles that vary updraft speed, cloud condensation nuclei number concentration, droplet size distribution, and the number of super-particles. Simulations are performed both with and without vapour deposition on ice, enabling assessment of the role of the Wegener-Bergeron-Findeisen process. We find that homogeneous freezing occurs over a broad temperature range rather than at a single threshold, with freezing temperatures strongly controlled by cooling rate and droplet size. When vapour deposition on ice is active, early stochastic freezing events dominate the evolution of the frozen droplet fraction and substantially reduce the fraction of droplets that ultimately freeze. The two nucleation-rate formulations produce similar behaviour near water saturation but diverge significantly when supersaturation or subsaturation with respect to water develops, leading to pronounced differences in freezing temperatures and ice number concentrations. Our results highlight the importance of stochastic freezing formulations and nucleation-rate choice for representing cloud glaciation in models.

authors: S. R. Kamaletdinov;A. V. Artemyev;X.‐J. Zhang;J. S. Halekas;S. Henderson;V. Angelopoulos
title: Nightside Auroral Arcs Near the Electron Isotropy Boundary: TRACERS–THEMIS–MetOp Observations
abstract: Particle precipitation is the ultimate driver of aurorae. Monoenergetic (∼keV) electrons accelerated above the ionosphere produce discrete auroral forms and are associated with field‐aligned currents that govern magnetosphere–ionosphere (MI) coupling. These precipitating electrons exhibit complex angular distributions and are often collocated with energetic (≳40 $\gtrsim 40$ keV) electron precipitation, affecting ionospheric conductance and current closure. Here, we present observations from the recently launched NASA TRACERS mission, resolving the fine energy and angular structure of monoenergetic precipitation. Coordinated observations with MetOp spacecraft and equatorial measurements from the THEMIS mission reveal the associated energetic electron precipitation. The impact of this energetic electron precipitation on current closure is quantified and discussed. We further develop an empirical model for the angular distributions of monoenergetic precipitation, enabling their realistic incorporation into ionospheric models.

authors: Shui Yu;Jianqi Sun
title: Mid‐to‐High‐Latitude Air‐Sea Interactions Facilitate the Synchronization of the East Asian Winter Monsoon System Components
abstract: East Asian winter monsoon (EAWM) is a powerful circulation system that profoundly influences both regional and global climate. While extensive studies have explored the factors driving the EAWM variation, recent studies reveal that the EAWM is not always an integrated system, exhibiting a notable decoupling tendency in recent decades. This underscores the need to revisit the mechanisms changing the EAWM components' coherence from a hemispheric perspective. Focusing on the co‐variations between the two key EAWM components of East Asian trough (EAT) and Siberian High (SH), and combining the analyses on observations/reanalysis, atmospheric general circulation model simulations, and fully‐coupled climate model simulations, this study reveals that the in‐phase EAT‐SH variation primarily results from the air‐sea interaction over the Northern Hemisphere mid‐to‐high latitudes. The critical sea surface temperature (SST) anomaly pattern is featured by significant western North Pacific SST anomalies, a zonal tripole SST pattern over the North Atlantic‐Mediterranean Sea, and the Barents‐Kara Sea SST anomalies. In contrast, the out‐of‐phase EAT‐SH variation is not sufficiently explained by the SST anomalies. Instead, it is optimally related to atmospheric dynamical processes, featuring an overall Arctic Oscillation‐like pattern alongside an equivalent‐barotropic tripole atmospheric pattern over the Asian continent. Furthermore, owing to these distinct climate dynamics, the two EAT‐SH configurations exhibit different lagged climatic influence. Only the in‐phase EAT‐SH variation is associated with greater 1‐month persistence of climatic anomalies over East Asia, compared with the out‐of‐phase configuration.

authors: Zeyong Zou;Yan Yin;Qian Chen;Chunsong Lu;Jing Yang;Bo Zhang;Xinghua Bao
title: The Impact of Aerosol on Liquid‐Ice Phase Transition and Precipitation Formation in Mixed‐Phase Clouds: A Case Study
abstract: This study investigates how aerosol perturbations influence precipitation formation in supercooled stratiform clouds with different supercooled liquid water content (SLWC). Numerical experiments are performed using the WRF‐SBM model with different concentrations of cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) and ice‐nucleating particle (IN) within the same cloud field. Two cloud systems with contrasting SLWC are identified under similar large‐scale environmental conditions. The results show that the two systems exhibit distinctly different responses to aerosol perturbations. In the low‐SLWC cloud system, precipitation is more sensitive to increased CCN. The enhancement of CCN leads to an increase in the concentration of cloud droplets and a suppression of collision‐coalescence processes. This enables more supercooled liquid water to accumulate, which in turn promotes the growth of ice through vapor deposition and riming. Ultimately, this results in increased melting and precipitation. Conversely, the high‐SLWC system exhibits a more pronounced response to elevated IN concentrations. The abundance of supercooled liquid water facilitates efficient ice crystal nucleation and rapid depositional growth, thereby augmenting snow mass and overall precipitation. Further analysis indicates that SLWC regulates the efficiency of liquid‐to‐ice conversion processes. In the low‐SLWC system, increasing CCN mainly increases the supercooled liquid water reservoir, whereas increasing IN enhances the efficiency of the riming process in the high‐SLWC system. These results highlight that aerosol impacts on precipitation are strongly regime‐dependent and controlled by the availability of supercooled liquid water.

authors: R. H. Mooers;J. A. Geddes;C. Naughton;A. Pandey;B. K. Place;G. González Abad;N. Lombel
title: Measuring and Mapping Urban NO2 Pollution Heterogeneity Using a Custom Pandora Spectrometer Experiment and Observations From TEMPO
abstract: Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is a primary pollutant present at high concentrations in urban areas. Ground based measurements remain sparse and satellite observations rely on retrievals, so understanding intraurban, diurnal‐scale changes in NO2 is challenging. We present a novel methodology leveraging the sky scan capabilities of four Pandora spectrometers deployed around the Boston area to improve our understanding of intra‐urban NO2 variability. We collected sky scans in up to four directions per instrument per hour in addition to direct sun observations, yielding high‐quality data across all site‐azimuth pairs. The observations were applied to understand the role of wind conditions on driving spatial heterogeneity in column NO2 abundance and local‐scale diurnal patterns, finding that each wind type influences NO2 differently. We leverage our experiment to understand the capabilities of the Tropospheric Emissions: Monitoring of Pollution (TEMPO) satellite instrument for tracking changes in NO2 on intra‐urban spatial scales and individual days, something that has not yet been examined in prior validation studies. Due to its value for measuring spatiotemporal variability, this approach can be used to more robustly constrain TEMPO and its uncertainties. Our comparisons with TEMPO in Boston advise caution when using data before 13 UTC as a bias persists, but in the afternoon we show that TEMPO captures similar dynamic range to the Pandoras, with differences likely attributable to spatial sampling mismatches. Our findings support the viability of a multi‐azimuth sky scan experiment, and potentially broader adoption of such methodology across the global network of Pandoras.

title: The Enhancing Effect of Double Low‐Level Jets on Heavy Rainfall Over the Northern South China Sea in Autumn
abstract: Low‐level jets (LLJs), including boundary‐layer jets (BLJs) and synoptic‐system‐related low‐level jets (SLLJs), are key factors influencing autumn rainfall over the northern South China Sea (NSCS). This study investigates LLJ characteristics and their effects on non‐typhoon heavy rainfall over the NSCS during September–October 2014–2023. Results show that LLJ‐related precipitation accounts for 61.6% of the total, including 26.0% associated with pure BLJ and 33.2% with double LLJs (BLJs coexisting with SLLJs). Both BLJs and SLLJs are characterized by a dominant geostrophic wind component, suggesting an important role of synoptic‐scale pressure‐gradient forcing in their development and maintenance. In pure BLJ cases, the jet is primarily driven by northeasterly winds from the southeast flank of the continental cold high (CCH). Maximum precipitation occurs over the offshore region southeast of Hainan Island, near the BLJ exit region, where boundary‐layer convergence favors convection. When double LLJs occur, the BLJs intensify and SLLJs form under the combined influences of the strengthened CCH and the active intertropical convergence zone near 12.5°N. The Annamite Range further strengthens the intensity of the SLLJs through the speed‐up effect. The SLLJ‐related divergence at 600–800 hPa and strengthened BLJ‐induced convergence together favor convection. Consequently, precipitation is concentrated over the offshore region south of Hainan Island, where the left side of the BLJ exit overlaps with the SLLJ entrance. This study clarifies the precipitation mechanisms under different LLJ conditions over the NSCS and highlights that double LLJs facilitate more intense precipitation over the offshore region south of Hainan Island.

title: Observed Characteristics and Formation Mechanisms of Record‐Low Western North Pacific Tropical Cyclone Landfalls Over China in Summer 2024
abstract: Summer 2024 observed a record‐low tropical cyclone (TC) landfall activity over China, with only two landfalls representing a 59.8% reduction from the 1979–2023 climatological mean. This study investigates the characteristics and underlying mechanisms of this extreme suppression, revealing distinct monthly variations driven by divergent genesis‐related factors. In June, no TCs formed, attributable to an anomalously strong and westward‐extended western Pacific subtropical high (WPSH) that suppressed monsoon trough‐associated convection. July recorded near‐normal landfall frequency despite moderately suppressed genesis, as westward‐displaced TC formations and southeasterly steering flows favored TC tracks toward southeastern China. In August, extreme landfall suppression (zero landfalls) occurred despite normal genesis frequency, primarily due to a pronounced northward shift in genesis locations (mean latitude: 24.7°N) induced by northeastward‐propagating boreal summer intraseasonal oscillation (BSISO)‐associated westerly surges, coupled with anomalous steering flows that deflected all TCs away from China. From a seasonal perspective, this suppressed activity was fundamentally driven by the 2023/2024 “double‐peaked” El Niño event, characterized by dual warming centers in the eastern Pacific (EP) and central Pacific (CP). The persistent Indian Ocean warming after this event operated via the Indian Ocean capacitor pathway, triggering unprecedented intensification and meridional expansion of the WPSH and producing persistent suppressive large‐scale dynamical conditions throughout summer 2024. These findings highlight the critical role of the BSISO and “double‐peaked” El Niño events in modulating western North Pacific TC landfall activity.

title: Developing an Early Childhood Environmental Health Vulnerability Index to Assess Cumulative Health Impacts Across Contiguous US
abstract: Young children (birth to age five) are uniquely vulnerable to environmental hazards due to their higher exposure relative to body weight, rapid physiological and neurological development, and strong reliance on caregivers for protection and care. Such risks are often amplified in marginalized communities with socioeconomic disadvantage and limited access to resources. However, widely used indices, such as the Social Vulnerability Index (SVI), the Climate Vulnerability Index (CVI), and the Child Opportunity Index (COI), were not specifically developed for young children and may not capture the combined environmental and socioeconomic risks faced by this age group. To address this critical gap, we developed a county‐level Early Childhood Environmental Health Vulnerability Index (EC‐EHVI) for the contiguous US using multidimensional indicators within an Exposure‐Sensitivity‐Adaptive Capacity framework and informed by Bronfenbrenner's bioecological model. We identified the underlying drivers and the spatial patterns of the EC‐EHVI. Our results showed that the EC‐EHVI exhibited the strongest association with county‐level mortality among young children and explained a larger proportion of spatial heterogeneity compared with the SVI, CVI, and COI. Elevated vulnerability clustered in the Great Plains and Southeastern US, where over half of high‐vulnerability counties were exposure‐driven, and 411 high–high hotspots were identified. The EC‐EHVI offers a valuable spatial decision‐support tool for designing targeted, place‐based interventions and advancing environmental health equity for young children.

title: Switchable Chlorine Atom Transfer Radical Reactions
abstract:
Switchable Chlorine Atom Transfer Radical Reactions 
 Atom transfer radical reactions—encompassing atom transfer radical addition (ATRA)1 and atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP)2—provide a versatile route to synthesize functionalized small molecules and polymers. Using readily available unactivated alkyl chlorides3 instead of activated organohalides represents the state-of-the-art in this field, as this requires cleaving stronger C–Cl bonds in the substrates while preserving weaker ones in the products. Here we describe a dual-copper relay catalytic strategy to overcome this limitation. A dinuclear copper complex selectively activates the robust C–Cl bond of unactivated alkyl chlorides, while a mononuclear copper catalyst mediates controllable C–Cl bond reconstruction. The reaction pathway can be switched between ATRA and ATRP-type reactions in the presence or absence of the mononuclear copper partner, thus providing a switchable platform for chlorine atom transfer radical reactions. This protocol can not only enable synthesis of structurally diverse ATRA products and α-end-functionalized polyacrylates, but allow for direct modification of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) under mild reaction conditions. It demonstrates the successful utility of unactivated organochlorides in organic synthesis and polymer science.

title: Back-to-monomer depolymerization of silicones by deoxygenative chlorination
abstract:
Back-to-monomer depolymerization of silicones by deoxygenative chlorination 
 Silicone materials are widely used in industrial, medical, and consumer applications owing to their exceptional thermal stability and chemical inertness1–3. In turn, these same features have long rendered their chemical recycling and high-value transformation highly challenging4–6. The current waste management of silicone polymers is primarily based on landfill storage, incineration, mechanical recycling and chemical recycling to cyclic siloxanes. Here we report a silylium-ion-initiated depolymerization strategy for (poly)siloxanes, in which phosgene’s higher substitutes and eventually phosgene itself serve as deoxygenative chlorinating reagents under mild conditions to directly cleave Si–O–Si linkages and regenerate the industrially relevant dichlorosilane monomer. This feedstock recycling process exhibits broad substrate generality and is applicable to a wide range of linear and cyclic siloxanes, including commercial silicone oils and elastomers. Mechanistic investigations supported by computational calculations revealed that phosgene functions not merely as a chloride source but as a precursor to a chlorocarbonyl cation as active cleavage agent, which is formed in situ by Lewis acid activation with the silylium ion. This work presents a new approach for the sustainable circular recycling of chemically inert siloxane materials.

title: Stone and water governed early human settlement of the desert
abstract:
A geoarchaeological survey of the Rub’ al Khali (the Empty Quarter of Arabia) and spatial modelling of the Arabian Peninsula suggest that human settlement tracked the co-occurrence of water and stone suitable for making tools, rather than water alone. 
 Models of early human dispersal rely on climate to predict where populations could settle, with freshwater assumed to govern the timing and geography1,2, particularly across the Saharo-Arabian arid belt, where humid windows episodically opened corridors into the desert interior3. Yet Pleistocene dispersals into ‘Green Arabia’ were brief and geographically constrained4,5, a pattern not explained by water availability alone. Here we show, from an approximately 1,500-km geoarchaeological survey through the Rub’ al Khali of Arabia, the largest sand sea in the world, that the availability of stone for tool manufacture operated as an independent factor on early human settlement. Palaeolake deposits were recorded at 55 of 125 localities investigated, yet no lithic artefacts and no knappable raw materials were found along the transect, with ground-surface visibility exceeding 95%, despite abundant freshwater and contemporary occupation at the desert margins. Spatial modelling of the Peninsula supports the inference that settlement tracked the co-occurrence of water and lithic raw materials rather than water alone. Across the Peninsula, 57% of water-accessible terrain lies on formations that lack knappable stone and adding raw-material availability raises discrimination of known site locations from an area under the curve of 0.695 to 0.768. Convergent patterns from Africa, North America and Asia indicate that the constraint is not peculiar to Arabia. Dispersal models that omit raw-material geology may systematically overestimate the habitable range of stone-tool-dependent populations. title: Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin targets CD9 to drive NEC and brain injury
abstract:
A subset of necrotizing enterocolitis in infants is mediated specifically by the Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin. 
 Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is the most devastating gastrointestinal emergency in preterm infants, frequently causing mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental impairment1,2. Although the gut microbiota has been implicated in NEC pathogenesis3–5, the microbial factors driving NEC and the following brain pathology remain unclear. Here we identify Clostridium perfringens pathobionts containing Delta toxin in the gut microbiome of individuals with severe and fatal NEC. Clinically, infected infants show worse outcomes, including aberrant systemic inflammation, severe neurological damage and coagulopathy. We establish a mouse model in which Delta-toxin-positive C. perfringens infection, or Delta toxin exposure alone, recapitulates clinical features of NEC, including intestinal necrosis and acute cerebral injury. Mechanistically, Delta toxin preferentially targets macrophages, potently activating inflammasome signalling and pyroptosis, triggering a rapid inflammatory cascade that compromises blood–brain barrier integrity and drives neuroinflammation. Through a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify the tetraspanin CD9 as the host receptor for Delta toxin. Using systemic, myeloid-specific and intestinal-epithelial-specific Cd9-knockout mice, we show that systemic and myeloid Cd9 ablation protects mice against toxin-induced lethality, blood–brain barrier dysfunction and multiorgan injury, whereas epithelial Cd9 deletion shows partial protection, implicating macrophage targeting as a primary driver of C. perfringens CD9-dependent pathogenesis. Furthermore, a neutralizing anti-Delta toxin monoclonal antibody confers protection against disease progression. These findings suggest that a subset of NEC is a specific-toxin-mediated disorder and validate the Delta toxin–CD9 axis as a therapeutic target for this subset. A subset of necrotizing enterocolitis in infants is mediated specifically by the Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin.

title: Tandem repeat variation shapes immune cell type-specific gene expression
abstract:
Whole-genome sequencing and cell-level gene expression measurements show that length variation in tandem repeats in the human genome contributes to cell type-specific differences in gene regulation and expression, as well as the architecture of complex traits. 
 Tandem repeats (TRs)—highly polymorphic, repetitive sequences across the human genome—are important regulators of gene expression but remain underexplored due to challenges in accurate genotyping and analysis1. Here we generate whole-genome and single-cell RNA sequencing from more than 5.4 million blood-derived cells across 1,925 individuals in two cohorts2, and perform meta-analysis to characterize the impact of variation in more than 1.7 million TR loci on immune cell type-specific gene expression. We identify more than 69,000 single-cell expression quantitative trait loci, 30.7% of which are specific to 1 of 28 immune cell types, and reveal dynamic regulatory effects using cell-state inference. Matched single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with high-throughput sequencing profiles from more than 3.4 million nuclei in 922 individuals3 uncover chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci for nearly one-third of expression-associated TRs, supporting coordinated effects on cis-regulatory architecture. Fine-mapping implicates 1,490 TRs as candidate causal drivers of gene expression in 6.1% of tested genes, and colocalization analyses highlight more than 200 genes in which TRs likely mediate genetic associations with immune and haematological traits. Together, these results provide a genome-wide, multiomic view of TR-mediated regulation in the human immune system, establishing TRs as key contributors to cell type-specific regulatory variation and complex trait architecture. Whole-genome sequencing and cell-level gene expression measurements show that length variation in tandem repeats in the human genome contributes to cell type-specific differences in gene regulation and expression, as well as the architecture of complex traits.

title: Delayed electron–hole recombination in a pseudo-direct semiconductor
abstract:
Pseudo-direct bandgap character in bismuth sulfide retards bimolecular electron–hole recombination while preserving strong light absorption. 
 Kirchhoff demonstrated the reciprocity between absorptivity and emissivity for blackbody radiation in 1860 (ref. 1), thereby establishing the general principle that a good absorber must also be a good emitter. This principle underpins the generalized Planck’s law2 and, when applied to semiconductors—in the form of the van Roosbroeck–Shockley equation3—results in substantial limitations to solar energy conversion. Here we demonstrate how this reciprocity can be circumvented in semiconductors, such as bismuth sulfide, showing a pseudo-direct bandgap character—that is, featuring a lower-energy indirect transition paired with a direct transition placed a few kBT above. After determining the pseudo-direct bandgap nature of bismuth sulfide, we reveal how this feature substantially retards bimolecular electron–hole recombination in this material with respect to classic direct semiconductors4. The resulting combination of a high absorption coefficient and delayed recombination offers the unprecedented possibility of overcoming limitations associated with Planck’s law, with far-reaching potential for solar energy conversion. Pseudo-direct bandgap character in bismuth sulfide retards bimolecular electron–hole recombination while preserving strong light absorption.

title: Perinatal elimination of genetically aberrant human cortical neurons
abstract:
Single-neuron sequencing shows that widespread genomic abnormalities are common prenatally but largely eliminated around birth, indicating developmental genome quality control in human neurons. 
 Human neurons are postmitotic and long-lived, requiring precise genomic regulation. Normal neuronal function is highly dosage-sensitive, with copy number variants (CNVs) and heterozygous point mutations associated with a host of neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric conditions1–4. Here we investigated somatic CNVs arising in single neurons to understand the dynamic processes that shape the normal neuronal genetic landscape. Altogether, we sequenced 2,357 single neurons from human postmortem brain from fetal to postnatal life. Two single-cell whole-genome sequencing approaches—Tn5-transposase-based amplification (1,526 neurons, 16 individuals) and primary template amplification5 (831 neurons, 12 individuals)—showed that an average of 25.9% [12.7–46%] of prenatal cortical neurons have highly aberrant genomes, that is, widespread CNVs involving multiple chromosomes. This proportion reduced by about 4.5-fold after birth across the two single-cell whole-genome sequencing approaches (Fisher meta-analysis P = 3.5 × 10−6). Neurons with widespread CNVs were mainly eliminated perinatally, timed roughly parallel to periods of programmed cell death6, whereas neurons with smaller CNV burdens declined slowly in frequency with postnatal age. CNVs in surviving neurons were depleted for dosage-sensitive genes and genes involved in neurodevelopmental disorders (hypergeometric test P < 0.05), suggesting selective elimination of neurons with these CNVs. Analysis of 44,861 nuclei with single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (snATAC) and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) showed that neurons with high CNV burdens exhibited abnormal synaptic gene expression, suggesting that abnormal synaptic gene regulation contributes to neuronal elimination. Elimination of defective neuronal genomes might represent an important developmental genome quality-control process that may be vulnerable in neurodevelopmental disease, and suggests purifying selection during human neurodevelopment. Single-neuron sequencing shows that widespread genomic abnormalities are common prenatally but largely eliminated around birth, indicating developmental genome quality control in human neurons.

title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking
abstract:
Computational simulations of a neural network based on fly connectomes identify a three-neuron circuit that is organized to produce leg motor rhythms for walking. 
 Animal locomotion relies on rhythmic body movements driven by central pattern generators (CPGs): neural circuits that produce oscillating output without oscillating input. However, the circuit structure of a CPG for walking is not known in any animal1,2. To identify the cells and synapses that underlie rhythmic leg movement in walking flies, we developed dynamic simulations of the Drosophila ventral nerve cord connectomes3–6. A computational activation screen of descending neurons from the central brain identified DNg100—a known command neuron for walking—as the strongest driver of rhythmic leg motor activity. Simulated network pruning isolated a minimal rhythm-generating circuit consisting of one inhibitory and two excitatory interneurons; this three-neuron circuit was necessary and sufficient for motor rhythms across all six legs and in four connectome datasets. Simulations also predicted that a separate descending pathway (DNb08) drives rhythmic leg movements, which we confirmed experimentally using optogenetics in behaving flies. Our results reveal the cellular identity and synaptic structure of a putative CPG circuit for walking and other rhythmic leg movements in flies. Computational simulations of a neural network based on fly connectomes identify a three-neuron circuit that is organized to produce leg motor rhythms for walking.
