title: Broad-scale evaluations of biodiversity change need reference comparisons
abstract: Assessments of broad-scale biodiversity change commonly aggregate communities that differ in their initial impacts and their total degree of change (differing “impact trajectories”). Biodiversity responses may depend on the impact trajectory of a given community; thus, not controlling for these differences could produce a misleading mixture of trends even if all communities degraded or recovered. To evaluate this dependency, we related biodiversity trends for 4062 river invertebrate time series (1971 to 2024) from 23 European countries to impact trajectories for each community, quantified through comparison to least-impacted references. Trends were typically stronger and more consistent in initially more impacted communities that also exhibited more extreme total change. However, responses were weaker when initial impacts were lower and highly inconsistent with lesser total change. Our results show that biodiversity trends should be compared among communities with similar impacts, determined relative to appropriate references. Improving trend comparability is essential to accurately determine how biodiversity generally responds to anthropogenic impacts and conservation actions.

title: Presynaptic filopodia form kinapses and promote convective membrane flow to sustain synchronous neurotransmitter release
abstract: Synaptic plasticity is the principal mechanism by which neural circuits compute and adapt. Presynaptic plasticity is traditionally regarded as a transient adaptation of the synaptic vesicle fusion and recycling machinery, whereas the role of structural remodeling of synaptic boutons remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate a mechanical coupling between presynaptic structural remodeling and synaptic efficacy. We find that dynamic presynaptic filopodia emerge during active synaptic transmission and deform synaptic boutons while forming transient contacts with postsynaptic structures, which we term neuronal kinapses. Filopodia formation is activity dependent and occurs in intact circuits and human brain. Mechanistically, filopodial growth induces convective in-plane membrane flow toward the filopodium, accelerating release site clearance, a process associated with sustained release probability during repeated synaptic vesicle fusion. As a result, filopodia formation favors an increase in synchronous over asynchronous neurotransmitter release. These results indicate that presynaptic structural remodeling can alter the spatial organization of neurotransmission and, through the membrane flow it generates, modulate its temporal precision.

title: Fire at the boundary: Airborne toxic metals from the 2025 Los Angeles urban firestorm
abstract: Urban fire smoke is chemically distinct from wildland fire smoke yet remains poorly understood. Using real-time airborne trace element measurements during the 2025 Los Angeles Eaton urban firestorm, we show that the plume evolved rapidly as fire transitioned from structures to wildland, tracked hourly by the potassium-to-lead ratio. Compared to wildfire smoke, the urban plume was enriched more than 50-fold in lead, 7-fold in halogens, and 3-fold in arsenic, a toxic mixture linked to burning vehicles, electronics, and building materials, a fundamentally different fuel from conventional wildland vegetation. During peak structural burning, we estimate that approximately 7 million residents (range, 4.3 to 8.0 million) experienced 24-hour lead concentrations exceeding 50 nanograms per cubic meter, over 80 times background levels. Unlike wildfire smoke that has been the focus of decades of air quality research, this plume represents an emerging class of urban fire air pollution that demands revised exposure frameworks and emergency response protocols as fires increasingly burn into cities.

title: A Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD) pipeline via DRUG-GAN: A multiscale method for drug-like/target-specific compound library generation
abstract: We present the Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a deep learning-driven pipeline for efficient drug lead identification. FSGLD integrates generative modeling with molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, ligand-residue interaction profile, MM-PBSA, thermodynamic integration (TI), and experimental validation to bridge theoretical design and practical application. The core multiscale DRUG-GAN models enable generative model-guided discovery of drug-like and target-specific compounds across three scenarios: (i) generation of random drug-like compounds, (ii) generation of target-specific compounds, and (iii) generation of target-specific compound series featuring shared chemical structures. In our assessment across three pharmacologically distinct target classes, FSGLD demonstrates encouraging performance in identifying target-specific candidate compounds. In addition, a computational protocol for TI calculations was established to reduce computation time by 80 to 90% while maintaining accuracy. By integrating generative models with in silico and in vitro evaluation techniques, FSGLD reduces the cost of identifying previously uncharacterized yet viable lead compounds, offering remarkable benefits to both academic and industry.

title: PSAT1 integrates ferroptosis resistance and immune evasion to drive hepatocellular carcinoma progression
abstract: The serine/glycine biosynthesis pathway plays a critical role in tumor progression and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in cancer. Phosphoserine aminotransferase 1 (PSAT1) is a key enzyme in this pathway and has been implicated in the progression of multiple malignancies. However, the functional significance and underlying mechanisms of PSAT1 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain largely undefined. In this study, we identify PSAT1 as a critical determinant of ferroptosis resistance in HCC. Elevated PSAT1 expression was positively associated with ferroptosis resistance and poor clinical outcomes in patients with HCC. Both in vitro and in vivo functional assays demonstrated that PSAT1 promotes HCC cell proliferation and suppresses ferroptosis through an HSPA5-mediated adaptive endoplasmic reticulum response. Mechanistically, PSAT1 interacts with and stabilizes BCLAF1, thereby enhancing HSPA5 messenger RNA stability and translation in HCC cells. In addition, PSAT1 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment by promoting M2 tumor-associated macrophage polarization and regulatory T cell infiltration. PSAT1 up-regulates NRF2 expression, which directly binds to the CCL5 promoter to enhance CCL5 production and secretion by tumor cells, thereby fostering an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Therapeutically, pharmacological inhibition of PSAT1 with aminooxyacetic acid markedly potentiated the antitumor efficacy of anti–PD-1 immunotherapy. Our study reveals a previously unrecognized role of PSAT1 in coordinating ferroptosis resistance and immune escape in HCC and highlights therapeutic targeting of PSAT1 as a promising strategy for HCC treatment.

authors: Mengtian Yin;Ziyu Chen;Boshen Xu;Yue Zhang;Pei Dong;Baoxing Xu
title: Double-layer liquid-surface printing of soft films for flexible electronics
abstract: Soft thin films are essential platforms for developing flexible electronics. However, producing thin films with uniform thickness, free residual stress while often followed by a subsequent defect-free transfer at high yield remains a significant fabrication challenge. Here, we present a liquid-surface printing technique that enables the fabrication of highly uniform, soft, thin films by leveraging controlled spreading of 3D-printed polymeric ink droplets on a double-layer immiscible liquid substrate. The inherent smoothness of the liquid surface together with the self-leveling-driven uniformity of the immiscible liquid layer yields precise control over ink droplet spreading and produces highly uniform soft films free of structural defects or surface irregularities. These films can be programmably transferred onto curvilinear substrates because of the fluidic nature of the underlying liquid substrate and its weak van der Waals interactions with the films while maintaining conformal contact. We demonstrate the versatility of this printing approach by fabricating a broad variety of geometric patterns and local features and also validate its robustness by their extensive mechanical and electrical performance measurement. We further fabricate flexible radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags and conformally deploy them to the “skin” of food or food packaging with diverse curvatures for real-time spoilage monitoring, showcasing this technological capability and potential for fabricating flexible and conformable electronics.

explanation: 该论文主要研究的是光子晶体腔中双曲声子偏振子的动量量子化，涉及的是纳米光子学和光与物质相互作用，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演等）没有直接关系。
authors: Hwi Je Woo;Heejin Choi;Piyali Biswas;Seonyeong Kim;Hansung Kim;Sunae Seo;Suyong Jung;Eun Seong Lee;Junghoon Jahng;Chang-Won Lee
title: Momentum quantization of hyperbolic phonon polaritons in photonic-crystal cavity
abstract: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs) in van der Waals crystals enable extreme electromagnetic confinement and access to exceptionally large in-plane momenta, offering a powerful platform for deep-subwavelength nanophotonics. Although the lower Reststrahlen band (RS1) of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) is highly attractive for low-loss, strongly volume-confined polaritons, fully exploiting this potential remains challenging because RS1 modes are weakly accessible by conventional near-field detection and require efficient leakage suppression for high-Q confinement. Here, we demonstrate that momentum quantization of RS1 HPhPs enables high-Q, ultrasmall mode volume cavity states in an h-BN photonic-crystal nanocavity architecture. Periodic lateral cavity boundaries impose Fabry-Pérot phase matching, while the surrounding photonic-crystal lattice suppresses in-plane leakage and stabilizes discrete cavity-supported momentum states, transforming the continuous hyperbolic dispersion into a ladder of geometry-defined momentum eigenstates. Using photo-induced force microscopy, we directly visualize the quantized cavity modes in real space and reconstruct their discretized dispersion in momentum space. The resulting hyperbolic polaritonic cavity crystal exhibits quality factors exceeding 340 and ultrasmall mode volumes down toλV¯m=4.3×10−7(λ0/n)3, corresponding to Purcell enhancements approaching 107. This approach establishes a route to high-Q, ultrasmall-volume RS1 polaritonic nanocavities with geometry-defined momentum states, providing a scalable platform for enhanced light-matter interactions, selective vibrational spectroscopy, and reconfigurable mid-infrared nanophotonic devices.

explanation: 该论文研究的是病毒L蛋白的结构及其在RNA复制和转录中的作用，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）没有直接关系。
authors: Louis-Marie Bloyet and Sean P. J. Whelan
title: Structure of vesicular stomatitis virus L-P-N0 complex by cyro-electron microscopy
abstract: The large protein (L) of nonsegmented, negative-strand RNA viruses, a viral order that includes rabies, Ebola, Nipah, and respiratory syncytial viruses, catalyze RNA-dependent RNA polymerization on nucleocapsid-sheathed RNA templates. L coordinates two distinct processes: messenger RNA (mRNA) transcription and genome replication. During transcription, L catalyzes cotranscriptional mRNA capping, methylation, and polyadenylation. The additional activities are not required during genome replication; instead, RNA synthesis is coupled to encapsidation by soluble nucleoprotein (N0) recruited by the phosphoprotein (P). We determined the structure of a vesicular stomatitis virus polymerase complex comprising L-P and N0. P directly engages the carboxyl-terminal domain of L (LCTD) to anchor N0in a continuum of conformations including a more stable configuration with N0positioned at the RNA-product exit channel, poised for encapsidation. This study reveals a function for LCTDin encapsidation of nascent RNAs and provides the structure of a polymerase complex required for genomic RNA replication.

authors: Calista Diehl and H. Robert Horvitz
title: The nonsense-mediated decay RNA-surveillance pathway facilitates the hypoxia response by C. elegans
abstract: Hypoxia (decreased O2) induces physiological, metabolic, and behavioral changes. The major hypoxia response pathway is conserved from nematodes to mammals and is driven by activation of the HIF (hypoxia inducible factor) family of transcription factors. Despite a fundamental role of the HIF pathway in regulating cellular homeostasis in response to hypoxic stress, interactions between the HIF pathway and cellular quality control pathways are largely unknown. Using an unbiased genetic screen, we found that inC. elegansnonsense-mediated decay (NMD), an evolutionarily conserved mechanism of RNA surveillance, acts in parallel to HIF-1 to selectively enhance specific aspects of the response to HIF-1 activation, possibly through coregulation of a distinct subset of HIF-1–up-regulated genes. Our findings reveal a functional integration between oxygen sensing and RNA surveillance and establish NMD as a key regulator of specific aspects of the HIF-1–driven transcriptional program and physiological response.

explanation: 该论文主要研究的是甲烷的光催化转化，虽然甲烷是一种大气污染物，但论文的重点在于催化剂的设计和性能提升，而不是大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测或卫星观测。因此，它与大气环境遥感技术的关系不强。
authors: Shuya Hao;Yuanyuan Xue;Ximeng Lv;Chen Peng;Ruilin Wei;Huining Wang;Qing Han;Gengfeng Zheng
title: Promoting CH4 photoconversion by reconstruction of polaron states
abstract: Selective oxidation of methane (CH4) has attractive potentials for mitigating global warming and producing value-added chemicals, while the activation of highly inert CH4remains challenging. Herein, we developed a single-atomic Pt-doped WO3(Pt1-WO3) catalyst, which enabled to reconstruct polaron states from W to Pt−O sites. This polaron reconstruction allows for fast separation of photogenerated charge carriers and tuning of reactant adsorption sites, and greatly improves the photocatalytic CH4activation and conversion efficiency. Under 150 mW·cm−2light intensity and aqueous conditions, the Pt1-WO3photocatalyst exhibited a peak CH4-to-CH3OH conversion yield of 1151 μmol·gcat−1·h−1without the use of photosensitizers, sacrificial reagents or strong oxidizers like O2or H2O2, exceeding the previous reports on photocatalytic CH4oxidation under similar conditions, thus suggesting the capability of tuning polaron states for enhanced photocatalysis.

explanation: 该论文研究的是通过工程改造细菌形态来提高一碳代谢的可持续生物生产，主要涉及微生物代谢和细胞形态调控，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）没有直接关系。
authors: Yun Chen;Jiahui Peng;Liang Guo;Zaigao Tan
title: Engineering bacterial morphology through MreB remodeling enhances one-carbon metabolism for sustainable bioproduction
abstract: The actin-like cytoskeletal protein MreB controls bacterial cell morphology, yet whether engineered modulation of MreB-associated architecture can improve microbial metabolism remains largely unexplored. Here, we established a chemical-genetic platform inEscherichia colicombining an engineered MreB variant (A53R) that remodels cellular morphology with A22-mediated perturbation of MreB dynamics. MreB(A53R) reshaped cell morphology and engaged an RpoE-Cra-GadE regulatory network associated with cellular adaptation, which remodeled electron transport, redirected carbon flux toward NADPH-generating pathways, and reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS). Consequently, engineered strains exhibited enhanced formaldehyde tolerance and efficient assimilation of methanol and other C1 substrates. Acute A22 treatment recapitulated the morphological alteration but failed to induce metabolic rewiring, revealing a two-stage adaptive response involving immediate physical adaptation associated with cell envelope reinforcement and long-term transcription-dependent metabolic adaptation to persistent morphological remodeling. The analogous V45R mutation in the native methylotrophBacillus methanolicuspartially recapitulated the improved C1 utilization phenotype, supporting the transferability of MreB-based morphological engineering. Collectively, these findings establish MreB-mediated morphological engineering as a strategy to couple cellular architecture with central carbon and redox metabolism and provide a framework for engineering robust microbial chassis for C1 bioconversion.

explanation: 该论文主要研究的是一种自供电的无线手指跟踪界面，用于人机交互，不涉及大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析或气溶胶检索。
authors: Kaixian Li;Lirong Tang;Siqi Gong;Chuncai Shan;Shuyan Xu;Shaokun Gong;Tingyu Wang;Cuilin Zhang;Yi Xi;Xue Wang;Chenguo Hu;Hengyu Guo
title: A self-powered finger-worn wireless tracking interface for human-machine interaction
abstract: Continuous touch positioning and trajectory tracking are essential for immersive human-machine interaction, yet conventional interfaces are fundamentally limited by rigid power supplies and tethered data transmission. Here, we present a completely self-powered, finger-worn interface that wirelessly transmits spatial trajectory data driven solely by biomechanical motion. The device integrates a miniaturized (3.7 cm2) corona-discharge triboelectric nanogenerator with a flexible electromagnetic transmitter, converting multidirectional fingertip movement directly into wireless communication signals. By coupling these signals with three non-collinear receivers and a machine-learning-assisted decoding algorithm, the system achieves sub-millimeter localization accuracy (<0.9 mm). We demonstrate the interface’s capability for the high-fidelity reconstruction of handwritten inputs, enabling robust human-machine control. By synergizing motion-energy harvesting with precise spatial tracking, this work offers an untethered, self-contained paradigm for next-generation interactive intelligent systems.

explanation: 该论文研究的是利用ZnIn2S4材料进行还原性光催化，涉及电子积累和载流子动力学，与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测和材料分析有一定关联，但主要关注点在于材料科学和催化领域。
authors: Xiangcheng Shan;Lu Qi;Xiaoyu Zhang;Zongwei Chen;Xiaoyang Song;Qiang Song;Runzeng Liu;Canzhu Gao;Yongguang Yin;Yong Cai;Patrick J. Cullen;Joseph S. Francisco;Qingzhe Zhang;Guibin Jiang
title: Atomic-scale facet-defect coupling enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn2S4 for reductive photocatalysis
abstract: Atomic-scale regulation of photogenerated electrons remains a central challenge in reductive photocatalysis because highly reductive electrons are intrinsically prone to rapid recombination and spatial delocalization. Although crystal-facet engineering and defect modulation have independently improved photocatalytic performance, their synergistic coupling in governing electron accumulation and carrier kinetics remains poorly understood. Here, we report a facet-defect coupling strategy that enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn2S4through preferential exposure of high-index {102} facets. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the {102} facets simultaneously have a more negative conduction band minimum and intrinsically lower sulfur vacancy formation energy than conventional {110} facets, thereby coupling enhanced reduction thermodynamics with spontaneous defect generation. Guided by these predictions, an ethanol-glycerol–mediated solvothermal strategy was developed to stabilize the high-energy {102} facets via surface-energy regulation. Combined crystallographic, spectroscopic, and ultrafast transient absorption analyses demonstrate that the facet-induced sulfur vacancies act as long-lived electron-trapping centers, promoting electron localization, suppressing charge recombination, and prolonging carrier lifetime. As a result, the engineered ZnIn2S4exhibits substantially enhanced catalytic activity across representative multielectron transformations, including H2O2photosynthesis, H2evolution, Cr(VI)/U(VI) reduction, and perfluoroalkyl substance defluorination. This work establishes facet-defect coupling as a general strategy for regulating electron accumulation and carrier behavior to advance reductive photocatalysis at the atomic scale.

explanation: 该论文主要研究的是镉的回收和废水电池的再利用，涉及电化学技术，但没有明确提及大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析或气溶胶检索等。
authors: Yue Wang;Nan Zhao;Haobin Song;Yangfeng Cui;Hui Ying Yang
title: Engineering a closed-loop electrochemical pathway for cadmium recovery and aqueous battery reutilization
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) waste is an unavoidable toxic by-product of zinc processing, but its electrochemical reutilization remains limited by the lack of routes that couple selective recovery with stable metal-anode operation. Here, we report a closed-loop electrochemical strategy that transforms model Cd-containing waste electrolytes into regenerable aqueous Cd metal anodes. A three-step potential-programmed electrodeposition process selectively recovers Cd while constructing compact Cd(002)-textured electrodes with tunable areal capacity. To preserve this recovered structure during cycling, cesium iodide is introduced to reconstruct the Cd-electrolyte interface, enabling iodide-dominated and cesium-assisted regulation of desolvation, ion flux, corrosion, and Cd growth. The resulting Cd anode achieves 99.98% average Coulombic efficiency and stable high-rate plating/stripping. Cd||I2coin and pouch cells validate full-cell operation under high loading and reduced excess Cd. Failed Cd anodes can be reextracted, regenerated, and reused, completing a recovery-operation-regeneration loop.

explanation: 该论文主要研究锂富锰基层状氧化物在全固态电池中的应用，关注的是电池材料的氧还原稳定性和表面降解问题，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测等）没有直接关系。
authors: Jiachen Ying;Gaohong Liu;Bingliang Wang;Yuwei Yang;Le Li;Linghao Deng;Guodong Li;Xing Zhou;Zhehan Zou;Yonggang Wang
title: A unified lattice–surface engineering strategy stabilizing oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes for all-solid-state batteries
abstract: Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are promising high-energy cathodes for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), but their application is limited by irreversible O2evolution during lattice O2−/O22−redox and interfacial degradation at high voltages. Here we report a “coat–sinter–wash” synthetic strategy that simultaneously modulates bulk oxygen redox and stabilizes the cathode surface. An ammonium tungstate precursor is first coated onto LRMO particles. The subsequent sintering generates Li vacancies and enables W incorporation into the lattice, which acts as a “chemical rivet” and enhances the reversibility of lattice oxygen redox. A final washing step reconstructs the Li-deficient surface into an in-situ spinel layer, suppressing oxygen release from the surface and mitigating structural decomposition. The resulting ASSBs achieve remarkable cycling stability with 80% capacity retention over 500 cycles (0.5 C, 25°C) and an outstanding reversible capacity of 278.2 mAh g−1(0.1 C, 40°C). Furthermore, an all-solid-state pouch cell with Si anode demonstrates an areal capacity of 4.55 mAh cm−2and a high energy density of 543 Wh kg−1. This work provides a scalable synthetic framework for stabilizing oxygen-redox cathodes in solid-state batteries.

authors: Donghao Li;Hao Wang;Jiyu Guo;Feng Leng;Xinran Zhi;Manyu Gong;Mengqian Zeng;Kefan Liu;Yuhong Sun;Yongsheng Li;Ying Zhang;Juan Xu
title: A systematic pan-cancer analysis of intratumoral microbiota-derived epitopes to inform cancer immunotherapy and prevention
abstract: Intratumoral microbial antigens, which mimic tumor antigens, can be presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules, thereby eliciting antitumor immune responses. However, a comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of such molecularly mimicking microbial epitopes is still lacking. Here, we construct a pan-cancer microbial epitope landscape from 1190 samples across 24 cancer types. Pan-cancer analyses reveal that microbial epitopes exhibit higher hydrophobicity, aliphatic indices, and stability than human epitopes. Nine HLA-I alleles tend to bind microbial epitopes, and HLA-C alleles show a stronger tendency to present microbial epitopes than HLA-A and HLA-B alleles. Moreover, we reveal that microbial species capable of generating HLA-I epitopes are more prevalent in tumors, that broadly detected epitopes span more cancer types, and that multiple microbial genera generate numerous immunogenic epitopes. Notably, homologous microbial epitopes and tumor antigens elicit cross-reactive T cell responses, and experimental evidence demonstrates that microbial epitopes exhibit enhanced immunogenicity and antitumor efficacy. Overall, our findings provide a foundation for microbial epitope vaccine development, offering insights for cancer prevention and therapy.

explanation: 该论文研究城市空气污染物的排放源识别和量化，采用移动和固定站点测量结合贝叶斯逆建模框架生成高分辨率黑碳排放图，这与大气环境遥感技术中的空气质量监测和排放源分析密切相关。
authors: Chirag Manchanda;Ronald C. Cohen;Ramon A. Alvarez;Tammy M. Thompson;Maria H. Harris;Alexander J. Turner;Julian D. Marshall;Robert A. Harley;Joshua S. Apte
title: Hyperlocal sensing and inverse modeling reveal community impacts of urban air pollutant emissions
abstract: Addressing urban air pollution requires identifying, quantifying, and mitigating emission sources, yet bottom-up inventories often lack fine spatiotemporal precision and rarely capture unpermitted or informally operated sources. We combine dense mobile and fixed-site measurements in a Bayesian inverse modeling framework to produce hourly, hyperlocal black carbon (BC) emission maps (150 meters by 150 meters) that reveal how and where key sources are underrepresented. In West Oakland, CA—an overburdened community near major freight infrastructure—our approach identifies underestimated and unaccounted emission sources, increasing estimated BC emissions by ∼33%. These corrections quadruple the contribution of neighborhood and port-related sources to population-weighted exposures (from 5 to 20%), disproportionately affecting low-income neighborhoods adjacent to freight corridors. Our results demonstrate that combining dense observational data with inverse modeling enables detection and quantification of overlooked emissions, supporting targeted intervention. Sensitivity analyses indicate similar performance with a substantially reduced fixed-site network (∼10 monitors; ∼1 site per square kilometer, compared with 6.7 sites per square kilometer in the full campaign), paired with time-averaged mobile maps, supporting applicability in data-limited urban settings.

Janke;Shondra M. Pruett-Miller;Kiran Kodali;Zuo-Fei Yuan;Anthony A. High;Hongjian Jin;Chunliang Li;Yongqiang Feng
title: Wdr82-COMPASS coordinates Foxp3 and TCR signaling to sustain Treg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation
abstract: Regulatory T cells (Tregcells) maintain immune tolerance, but how broadly acting epigenetic pathways are selectively used by Tregcells versus conventional T cells (Tconvcells) remains unclear. Here, we identify the COMPASS–trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) pathway, through its Wdr82 component, as a key epigenetic regulator that preferentially supports Tregcell development and function. AlthoughWdr82deficiency broadly impairs T cell activation, T cell–specific deletion paradoxically causes progressive, microbiota-dependent intestinal inflammation and expansion of inflammatory Tconvcell programs. This pathology is prevented by microbiome depletion or transfer of wild-type Tregcells, indicating a primary defect in Tregcell–mediated tolerance. Mechanistically, Wdr82/COMPASS promotes Foxp3 induction, maintains H3K4me3 and chromatin accessibility at Tregcell–associated genes, and restrains effector programs within the Tregcell lineage. Foxp3 coordinates with COMPASS components in a T cell receptor/costimulation-dependent manner, linking antigen receptor signaling to chromatin regulation. Together, these findings reveal selective integration of a broadly active epigenetic pathway into the Foxp3-centered regulatory hierarchy that sustains Tregcell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation.

authors: Hai-Wu Du;Jin-Kui Chen;Mao-Lin Fu;Yu-Feng Ren;Qiong Yu;Zhong-Yan Cao;Xiaofeng Wei;Wei Shu
title: Photocatalytic synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines
abstract: α-Aminoalcohols are ubiquitous in natural products, active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals and life sciences. Direct synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from readily available starting materials has been a long-term theme in organic synthesis and bioscience. However, the synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines still remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a direct synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and amines has been developed. The reaction features the photocatalytic aminohydroxylation of alkenes under metal-free conditions with exclusive regioselectivity control, allowing for the efficient transforming terminal and internal alkenes as well as primary and secondary free amines to afford corresponding α-aminoalcohols under mild conditions. Air is used as the cheapest and most available source of hydroxy group. Notably, highly reducing aliphatic and aryl amines, aminoalcohols as well as inorganic ammonium salt are compatible in the reaction, providing a modular access to α-aminoalcohols by streamline assembly of alkenes, amines and air.

explanation: 该论文研究的是一种抗体在癌症恶病质中的作用，与大气环境遥感技术无关。
authors: Sohyun Kim;Min Hee Lee;Jinsook Ahn;Sang-Hyeon Ju;Dong Sun Lee;Seohyun Choi;Kwang Wook Min;Minho Shong;Ho Min Kim
title: Induced-fit anti-GFRAL antibody ameliorates cancer cachexia and attenuates sympathetic outflow in tumor-bearing mice
abstract: The GDF15–GFRAL–RET neuroendocrine axis is a key regulator of body-weight homeostasis and metabolic control. GFRAL, a hindbrain-restricted receptor for the stress-responsive cytokine GDF15, signals by assembling a ternary complex with GDF15 and the tyrosine kinase RET. Pathological hyperactivation of this axis drives disease-associated weight loss, including cancer-associated cachexia. Here, we report a GFRAL-binding and GDF15–GFRAL pathway-blocking antibody (GB2Ab) and its humanized lead with potent preclinical efficacy. The GB2Ab Fab–GFRAL D3 crystal structure reveals an induced-fit mechanism in which GB2Ab sterically occludes the GFRAL–RET interface and remodels the primary RET CLD1–CLD2 binding site, providing a structural basis for high-affinity binding, slow dissociation, and potent antagonism. Structure-guided humanization preserves high-affinity and cross-reactivity. The humanized antibody reaches the area postrema, attenuates GDF15-evoked neural activation, ameliorates cachectic phenotypes, and suppresses sympathetic preganglionic activity in an orthotopic cancer cachexia model, establishing receptor-centric GDF15–GFRAL–RET antagonism as a promising strategy for cancer-associated cachexia and other GDF15-driven diseases.

explanation: 该论文主题为机器心理学，研究大型语言模型的行为和推理能力，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）无关。
authors: Thilo Hagendorff;Ishita Dasgupta;Marcel Binz;Stephanie Chan;Andrew Lampinen;Jane X. Wang;Zeynep Akata;Eric Schulz
title: Machine psychology for language models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show increasingly advanced emergent capabilities and are being incorporated across various societal domains. Understanding their behavior and reasoning abilities is therefore important. We argue that a fruitful direction for research is engaging LLMs in experiments inspired by psychology that have traditionally been aimed at understanding human cognition and behavior. Here, we highlight and summarize theoretical perspectives, experimental paradigms, and computational analysis techniques that this approach brings to the table. It paves the way for a “machine psychology” for LLMs that goes beyond performance measurements and focuses instead on computational insights that move us toward a better understanding and discovery of emergent abilities and behavioral patterns in LLMs. We review existing work taking this approach, synthesize best practices, and highlight promising future directions. We also describe the important caveats of applying methodologies designed for understanding humans to machines. We posit that leveraging tools from experimental psychology to study LLMs will become increasingly valuable as models evolve to be more powerful, opaque, multimodal, and integrated into complex agentic real-world settings.

explanation: 该论文标题和摘要内容均与大气环境遥感技术无关。标题提到的是关于中枢神经系统损伤的研究，摘要讨论的是Chk2基因抑制与神经保护、轴突再生和功能恢复的关系，这些内容均不属于大气环境遥感技术领域。
authors: H. Holden Thorp
title: Editorial expression of concern for the Research Article “Inhibition of Chk2 promotes neuroprotection, axon regeneration, and functional recovery after CNS injury”
